publicEntries.title: HTTP/2 client stale-heap disclosure
publicEntries.summary: A response could reuse fragment metadata from the client request, and a premature fragmented response could leave that metadata pointing beyond initialized header storage. Upstream published complementary fragment-accounting and early state-rejection fixes, both with Reported-by credit.

evidence.primitive: Out-of-bounds read with stale client-heap disclosure
evidence.validation: ASan boundary report plus separate-process 5/5 trigger and 5/5 control
evidence.boundary: Tested on the cleartext HTTP/2 prior-knowledge client path; demonstrated effect is stale client-heap disclosure

publicEntries.credit: Original report by Ratnaker Gautam; both upstream fixing commits contain Reported-by credit

weakness.basis: Response decoding reused the request header fragment slot before the relevant state was rejected. Correcting fragment-slot accounting and rejecting premature response headers before decoding removes the observed ordering defect and later out-of-bounds read.

publicEntries.title: Security descriptor offset wrap on 32-bit kernels
publicEntries.summary: An authenticated SMB2 SET_INFO request could supply security-descriptor offsets beyond the descriptor. On 32-bit builds, forming pointers before validating those offsets could wrap them outside the descriptor and fault the kernel. The public fix validates each nonzero offset numerically before pointer arithmetic.

evidence.primitive: Out-of-range memory access after 32-bit offset wrap
evidence.validation: Authenticated network replay on i686, valid control, and patched-kernel replay
evidence.boundary: Authenticated SMB client against a 32-bit ksmbd server; demonstrated consequence is kernel denial of service

publicEntries.credit: Original report by Ratnaker Gautam; the maintainer commit contains Reported-by credit and is carried in linux-next

weakness.basis: Untrusted 32-bit offsets were added to the descriptor base before their range was validated. On 32-bit builds, that arithmetic could wrap the derived pointer outside the security descriptor.

publicEntries.title: Progressive hint object-number heap out-of-bounds write
publicEntries.summary: During progressive loading, the hint-repair path used an object number parsed from the PDF as an index into the hint offset table without checking it against the table size, so a crafted linearized PDF could direct an 8-byte heap write outside that table. Upstream's fix, published as an out-of-bounds read fix in hint handling, checks each object number against the table bounds before the table is read or written and abandons the hints when a number is out of range.

evidence.validation: ASan replays on then-current master and release 1.28.5 through the documented progressive-loading API, valid controls, 5/5 native guard-overwrite and allocator-abort replays, and patched replay
evidence.boundary: Requires an application that loads a crafted linearized PDF progressively; demonstrated effect is heap corruption next to the hint offset table

publicEntries.credit: Original report and patch by Ratnaker Gautam; the upstream fixing commit credits his report and patch

weakness.basis: An object number read from the file was used as a hint-table index without a bounds check. The resulting write outside the allocation was separately observed with AddressSanitizer; the public fix validates each object number against the table size before use.

publicEntries.title: Repeated SDP rtpmap handler-context leak
publicEntries.summary: Repeated mappings for one RTP stream replaced an allocated dynamic protocol context without releasing the previous one. The submitted patch closes and frees the current context before installing its replacement.

evidence.validation: LSan, public API loops, loopback RTSP, controls, and 209 enabled FATE tests
evidence.boundary: Measured consequence is persistent allocation growth under repeated mappings

publicEntries.credit: Original public patch authored and signed off by Ratnaker Gautam; maintainer review pending

primary.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

weakness.basis: A replacement allocation overwrote the only pointer to the prior live allocation, so teardown could no longer release it.

publicEntries.title: Multi-source callback-data double close
publicEntries.summary: When multiple callback-data objects are configured without a switch callback, crossing a source boundary invokes the owning close callback for the old object. Final teardown invokes it again for the same pointer. Two public pull requests propose fixes and reviewers requested changes on both; the open question is whether libarchive should reject this configuration or keep fallback semantics that close each object once.

evidence.primitive: Repeated owning close callback causing a heap double free
evidence.validation: Self-contained public-API ASan replay on current master, explicit-switch control, and split-input release reproduction
evidence.boundary: Requires multiple callback-data objects without a switch callback; maintainers regard that configuration as unsupported and requested public API discussion

publicEntries.credit: Original report, public issue, and pull request 3738 by Ratnaker Gautam; reviewers requested changes and the fix approach remains under discussion

weakness.basis: The source-transition fallback and final teardown both pass the same callback-data pointer to an owning close callback, causing the same allocation to be freed twice.

publicEntries.title: iSCSI R2T range-check integer overflow
publicEntries.summary: An iSCSI target can choose a 32-bit R2T data offset and length whose sum wraps before the client compares it with the SCSI data-buffer length. The wrapped range passes validation and can exhaust the command scatterlist before a NULL next entry is dereferenced. The public patch replaces the overflowing sum with ordered offset and remaining-length checks.

evidence.primitive: Unsigned range-check overflow followed by a NULL scatterlist dereference
evidence.validation: Target-driven i386 kernel-panic replay, matched control, exact patched replay, current-source build, and clean strict checkpatch
evidence.boundary: Requires a logged-in iSCSI session and a target-controlled R2T; maintainers regard targets as trusted and are handling this through the normal bug-fix process

publicEntries.credit: Public patch authored and signed off by Ratnaker Gautam; Acked-by review received from Chris Leech; upstream application pending

weakness.basis: The validation adds two attacker-controlled 32-bit quantities before comparing the result with the buffer length, allowing modular wraparound to make an out-of-range transfer appear valid.

publicEntries.title: Garbage-collecting save object-reference leak
publicEntries.summary: When a non-incremental save renumbered objects, it stored owned replacement objects through setters that keep their own references and then discarded the caller's reference without releasing it. Each garbage-collecting save could therefore retain an input-proportional amount of memory until a long-lived process reached its allocation limit. Upstream fixed the leak on master by releasing each replacement after it is stored.

evidence.primitive: Input-proportional memory retention on every garbage-collecting save
evidence.validation: ASan/LSan and Valgrind replays on then-current master, 1,000-save native RSS and address-space-limit replays, PyMuPDF ez_save replay, garbage-level-1 controls, and patched replay with byte-identical output
evidence.boundary: Requires repeated full saves with garbage collection at level 2 or 3 in a long-lived process; measured consequence is memory growth and eventual allocation failure

publicEntries.credit: Original report and patch by Ratnaker Gautam; the upstream fixing commit credits his report and patch

consequences.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

weakness.basis: Renumbering stored owned replacement objects through reference-keeping setters but never dropped the caller's reference, leaving one extra count per stored replacement. The resulting unreleased memory was separately measured with LeakSanitizer and process RSS; the public fix drops the caller's reference after each store.

publicEntries.title: RFC4175 incomplete-frame heap disclosure
publicEntries.summary: The campaign reproduced an incomplete-frame disclosure, then retired it after matching the behavior to an earlier public upstream fix. It is retained as validation work and excluded from original-finder totals.

evidence.primitive: Uninitialized heap data in decoded frame output
evidence.validation: Sanitizer and output-level reproduction matched to the public fix
evidence.boundary: Prior public discovery; no original finder or CVE claim

publicEntries.credit: Upstream fix credits Joshua Rogers and identifies AISLE-2026-0111-00477

weakness.basis: Incomplete packets left part of an allocated frame buffer uninitialized; zero-initializing the frame allocation removes the disclosed tail.

publicEntries.title: Cookie-cache lifetime violation
publicEntries.summary: The campaign independently reproduced the cache-result lifetime defect and its cross-origin behavioral consequence. Public history showed that the same defect had already been fixed, so the candidate was retired as an exact duplicate.

evidence.primitive: Heap use after free with stale cache result reuse
evidence.validation: Sanitizer reproduction and production-path behavior matched to prior fix
evidence.boundary: Prior public fix; retained only as independent validation

publicEntries.credit: The upstream fix predates this campaign's disclosure review

weakness.basis: Cache eviction freed the lookup result while the active walk retained and read its stale pointer.

publicEntries.title: Invalid progressive linearization page count
publicEntries.summary: The progressive-loading campaign reproduced the invalid page-count failure and then matched it to public Artifex Bug 709789 and its upstream correction. The result was removed from the new-report queue.

evidence.primitive: Invalid memory access during progressive PDF loading
evidence.validation: Reproduction matched against public bug and fixing commit
evidence.boundary: Prior public report; no original finder or CVE claim

publicEntries.credit: Publicly tracked by Artifex as Bug 709789

primary.name: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input

weakness.basis: The PDF-declared linear page quantity was used without enforcing a positive value; the public fix rejects non-positive counts before allocation.

publicEntries.title: AAPL CREATE response heap overflow
publicEntries.summary: An authenticated network replay independently reproduced a CREATE-response size error that crossed a kernel slab-object boundary. The maintainer identified an existing public fix, so this record documents validation rather than original discovery.

evidence.validation: KASAN network replay, maximal control, and patched-kernel replay
evidence.boundary: Exact public duplicate; KASAN corruption and denial of service independently reproduced

publicEntries.credit: Original public patch by Jérémy Jean; Ratnaker Gautam independently reproduced and reported it

weakness.basis: The CREATE response allocation omitted valid response-context sizes. The resulting write beyond the allocated response buffer was independently reproduced with KASAN.

publicEntries.title: Malformed Opus granule returns uninitialized heap bytes
publicEntries.summary: A decreasing end-of-stream granule position made the Opus reader expose more frames than the packet decoder produced. The extra samples came from a fresh, uninitialized allocation. Runtime validation confirmed the behavior on current source, but a 2019 code-review discussion had already identified the same branch, malformed-input condition, and data-exposure consequence.

evidence.primitive: Uninitialized heap contents copied through sf_readf_float
evidence.validation: Valgrind allocation origin, 20/20 native marker recovery, regular-file replay, and matched controls
evidence.boundary: Exact public prior art; no original-finder or CVE claim

publicEntries.credit: Arthur Taylor identified the defect and disclosure consequence in the 2019 review; Ratnaker Gautam independently validated current-source reachability

weakness.basis: The reader returned samples beyond the decoder-produced frame count from a freshly allocated, uninitialized buffer.

privateEntries.summary: Reports currently under maintainer review. Evidence, correspondence, and project-specific timelines are retained in the offline research record.

privateEntries.title: Candidates under review
privateEntries.summary: Candidate findings undergoing practical-impact, prior-art, or report-readiness review before any public claim is made.
